commits.message:
feat(taxonomy): inline edit for skill descriptions, with audit and AI-overwrite protection

Update-only, per spec: no separate delete -- clearing a description is
just editing it to empty.

app/understanding/taxonomy/loader.py: set_skill_description now takes
source ("ai_generated" | "human_edited") and edited_by, and stamps
description_source/description_edited_by/description_edited_at on the
entry. A human edit (source="human_edited") always wins, including over
another human's earlier edit -- last save wins is the expected behavior
for a shared admin field. An ai_generated write against an entry
already marked human_edited raises SkillDescriptionLocked instead of
silently overwriting it -- the actual mechanism behind "never let
auto-regeneration silently overwrite a human edit." No current caller
can hit this yet (approval-time auto-gen only ever calls add_canonical_
skill, which only ever creates NEW entries), but it's the real guard
for whenever a "regenerate" action exists.

update_skill_description() (app/understanding/taxonomy/candidates.py):
always calls set_skill_description with source="human_edited", so this
path can never itself be blocked -- it's the one making the edit, not
overwriting one. New PATCH /taxonomy/skills/description (app/routers/
moderation.py), name+description in the body rather than a path param
(skill names like "C++"/".NET" are needlessly fragile to URL-encode
correctly for what's already a POST-shaped admin action).

Frontend: SkillsTaxonomyPage's description cell is now editable inline
(pencil-style Edit link, textarea, Save/Cancel -- same interaction
pattern as the draft field-editing built earlier) and shows a small
"AI" or "edited" badge per description_source, with edited-by/edited-
at in a hover tooltip on the "edited" badge. Saves update the row in
place rather than reloading the whole table.

New coverage: a human edit stamps source/edited_by/edited_at correctly;
an ai_generated write against a human-edited entry raises
SkillDescriptionLocked and the original text survives; the real PATCH
endpoint updates a skill end-to-end; updating a nonexistent skill
reports failure rather than raising. Full regression suite (18 checks)
green. Frontend type-checks and builds clean.
